arxiv-2002-00239.title: Cohomology fractals
arxiv-2002-00239.creator: David Bachman, Saul Schleimer, Henry Segerman
arxiv-2002-00239.description: Abstract We introduce cohomology fractals; these are certain images associated to a cohomology class on a hyperbolic three-manifold. They include images made entirely from circles, and also images with no geometrically simple features. They are closely related to limit sets of kleinian groups, but have some key differences.

Many programming problems call for turning geometrical thoughts into code: tables, hierarchical structures, nests of objects, trees, forests, graphs, and so on. Linear text does not do justice to such thoughts. But, it has been the dominant programming medium for the past and will remain so for the foreseeable future.

arxiv-2101-01083.title: Topology of the energy landscape of sheared amorphous solids and the irreversibility transition
arxiv-2101-01083.creator: Ido Regev, Ido Attia, Karin Dahmen, Srikanth Sastry, Muhittin Mungan
arxiv-2101-01083.description: Abstract Recent experiments and simulations of amorphous solids plastically deformed by an oscillatory drive have found a surprising behavior - for small strain amplitudes the dynamics can be reversible, which is contrary to the usual notion of plasticity as an irreversible form of deformation.

arxiv-2101-08417.title: Zariski density of points with maximal arithmetic degree for surfaces
arxiv-2101-08417.creator: Kaoru Sano, Takahiro Shibata
arxiv-2101-08417.description: Abstract . We prove that any surjective self-morphism f f with δ f > 1 \delta_{f}>1 on a potentially dense smooth projective surface defined over a number field K K has densely many L L -rational points for a finite extension L / K L/K . 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 37P55, Secondary 14G05 1.

arxiv-2101-11943.title: An Explainable AI System for Automated COVID-19 Assessment and Lesion Categorization from CT-scans
arxiv-2101-11943.creator: Matteo Pennisi, Isaak Kavasidis, Concetto Spampinato, Vincenzo Schininà, Simone Palazzo, Francesco Rundo, Massimo Cristofaro, Paolo Campioni, Elisa Pianura, Federica Di Stefano, Ada Petrone, Fabrizio Albarello, Giuseppe Ippolito, Salvatore Cuzzocrea, Sabrina Conoci
arxiv-2101-11943.description: Abstract COVID-19 infection caused by SARS-CoV-2 pathogen is a catastrophic pandemic outbreak all over the world with exponential increasing of confirmed cases and, unfortunately, deaths. In this work we propose an AI-powered pipeline, based on the deep-learning paradigm, for automated COVID-19 detection and lesion categorization from CT scans.

arxiv-2109-04112.title: Constraints on the spatially dependent cosmic-ray propagation model from Bayesian Analysis
arxiv-2109-04112.creator: Meng-Jie Zhao, Kun Fang, Xiao-Jun Bi
arxiv-2109-04112.description: Abstract The energy spectra of primary and secondary cosmic rays (CR) generally harden at several hundreds of GeV, which can be naturally interpreted by propagation effects. We adopt a spatially dependent CR propagation model to fit the spectral hardening, where a slow-diffusion disk (SDD) is assumed near the Galactic plane.

arxiv-2209-00249.title: Radio Localization and Sensing – Part II: State-of-the-art and Challenges
arxiv-2209-00249.creator: Henk Wymeersch, , Gonzalo Seco-Granados
arxiv-2209-00249.description: Abstract This letter is part of a two-letter tutorial on radio localization and sensing, with a focus on mobile radio systems, i.e., 5G and beyond. Building on Part I, which focused on the fundamentals, here we go deeper into the state-of-the-art advances, as well as 6G, covering enablers and challenges related to modeling, coverage, and accuracy.

arxiv-2311-06304.title: Retro-BLEU: Quantifying Chemical Plausibility of Retrosynthesis Routes through Reaction Template Sequence Analysis
arxiv-2311-06304.creator: Junren Li, Lei Fang, Jian-Guang Lou
arxiv-2311-06304.description: Abstract Computer-assisted methods have emerged as valuable tools for retrosynthesis analysis. However, quantifying the plausibility of generated retrosynthesis routes remains a challenging task. We introduce Retro-BLEU, a statistical metric adapted from the well-established BLEU score in machine translation, to evaluate the plausibility of retrosynthesis routes based on reaction template sequences analysis.

arxiv-2403-06311.title: How much data do you need? Part 2: Predicting DL class specific training dataset sizes.
arxiv-2403-06311.creator: Thomas Mühlenstädt, Jelena Frtunikj
arxiv-2403-06311.description: Abstract Abstract This paper targets the question of predicting machine learning classification model performance, when taking into account the number of training examples per class and not just the overall number of training examples. This leads to the a combinatorial question, which combinations of number of training examples per class should be considered, given a fixed overall training dataset size.

arxiv-2505-01991.title: Very standard homogeneous Finsler manifolds with positive flag curvature
arxiv-2505-01991.creator: Xiyun Xu, Ming Xu
arxiv-2505-01991.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Xiyun Xu, Ming Xu. In this paper, we consider a homogeneous manifold G / H G/H in which G G is a compact connected simply connected simple Lie group and H H is a closed connected subgroup of G G . We define standard and very standard homogeneous Finsler metrics on G / H G/H , which generalize the standard homogeneous ( α 1 , α 2 ) (\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}) metric in literature.

arxiv-2510-25177.title: Temperature-Gradient Effects on Electric Double Layer Screening in Electrolytes
arxiv-2510-25177.creator: Kazuhiko Seki
arxiv-2510-25177.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kazuhiko Seki. Temperature gradients drive asymmetric ion distributions via thermodiffusion (Soret effect), leading to deviations from the classical Debye–Hückel potential. We analyze non-isothermal electric double layers using dimensionless Soret coefficients α ± \alpha_{\pm} (for cations and anions, respectively). Analytical solutions of the generalized Debye–Hückel equation show that, for α + = α − \alpha_{+}=\alpha_{-} , the potential is exactly described by a modified Bessel function, while the marginal case α ± = 1 \alpha_{\pm}=1 exhibits algebraic decay.

pmc-10571515.title: The Role of Autophagy in Brain Tumors
pmc-10571515.creator: Gabriella D’Orazi
pmc-10571515.description: Autophagy is a highly conserved cellular homeostatic process that maintains cellular homeostasis through the degradation, elimination, and recycling of damaged substrates, such as organelles, macromolecules, and misfolded proteins [3]. However, its deregulation is associated with several pathological processes, including cancer [4]. It has been demonstrated that autophagy has a double role, both as a tumor promoter and as a suppressor.

pmc-11362453.title: Association of total bilirubin and prognosis in disorders of consciousness
pmc-11362453.creator: Laigang Huang, Li Zhang, Dongmei Gao, Min Sun, Wenhan An, Qiangsan Sun, Fanshuo Zeng, Baojuan Cui
pmc-11362453.description: Accurate prediction of the recovery of Disorders of Consciousness (DoC) is of paramount significance for clinicians and families. Serum total bilirubin (TBIL) formed by activation of heme oxygenase 2, is associated with incidence and prognosis of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. However, studies that based TBIL and DoC are limited.

pmc-12470698.title: Foraging Behaviors and Comparative Yield Effects of Bumblebee (Bombus terrestris Linnaeus) and Chinese Honeybee (Apis cerana cerana Fabricius) to Cherry (Prunus pseudocerasus ‘Hongdeng’) in Northern China
pmc-12470698.creator: Xunbing Huang, Yueyue Wang, Li Zheng, Simona Sagona, Kit S Prendergast
pmc-12470698.description: Simple SummaryBees are the most widely used managed crop pollinators. This study evaluated the foraging behavior and pollination effect of bumblebee Bombus terrestris and Chinese honeybee Apis cerana cerana on cherries (Prunus pseudocerasus ‘Hongdeng’) in northern China. Bee pollination significantly improved cherry production. The daytime foraging activity and pollen-carrying capacity of bumble bees were different from Chinese honeybees.

pmc-13465910.title: Integrating Imaging Markers for Clinical Risk Stratification of Takotsubo Syndrome
pmc-13465910.creator: Liya Dai, Yuyi Chen, Frank Seghatol, Han Tang, Crystal Licari, Sabrina Vaughn, Juan Lei, Amanda Chang, Silma Subah Raisa, Xiaodong Wu, Kan Liu
pmc-13465910.description: Background:The purpose of this study was to develop machine learning (ML) models that integrate clinical and echocardiographic markers to predict adverse cardiovascular events in patients with Takotsubo syndrome (TTS).Methods:ML-based prediction models were developed on the basis of 2 retrospective data sets comprising 450 TTS patients (252 in an internal cohort and 198 in an external cohort).

pmc-13675434.creator: Yan Ren, Can Cui, Zhijing Zhang, Wei Liao, Chen Zhang, Yue Cheng, Wen Shen
pmc-13675434.description: ObjectiveTo develop a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance.Materials and methodsThe modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was developed by incorporating the significant signs from the standard O-RADS MRI system.
